## Motivation

A certificate of deposit (CD) holds money for a specified term. Its annual
percentage yield (APY) expresses the annualized return with compounding.
Credit unions offer a similar product called a share certificate.

Does a longer term have a higher quoted APY? Do the distributions differ
between banks and credit unions? These data allow students to compare the
answers from two different samples: all institutions observed at each term,
and the subset observed at both terms.

## Data

The CSV contains 3,013 institution-term observations from 436 independent
regulators at nine terms. It was extracted without filtering or imputation
from the `samples` array in APY Ledger's public October 23, 2026 release.
Each row is one selected quote, not one customer account or one depositor.

For each regulator and exact term, the selection uses the highest qualifying
quote for a $10,000 deposit, excludes relationship-only offers and requires a
known applicable deposit tier. If more than one observed ZIP qualifies, the
highest APY is selected. The source quotes were verified within seven days
of export, not all at one instant.

This is a selected observational sample, not a census or a random sample of
U.S. institutions. High quoted APYs can have membership, residency, new-money
or other opening conditions. A blank ZIP means that no sample ZIP was
recorded for that quote; it does not establish nationwide availability.
An absent institution-term row is not a zero rate. Institutions observed at
different terms can differ, and rows for one regulator are not independent
institutions. Source checks can miss errors; these are historical observations,
not current offers or investment recommendations.

### Variable descriptions

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| regulator_id | FDIC or NCUA identifier; use this to join terms within an institution. |
| type | `bank` or `credit_union`. |
| slug | Publisher's readable institution identifier. |
| term_days | Exact term in days; 365 is one year and 1825 is five years. |
| term_label | Source term label for readers. |
| apy | APY in percentage units: 3.5 means 3.5%, not 0.035. |
| min_deposit | Published minimum deposit tier in U.S. dollars. |
| product | Selected product name. |
| kind | Offer label, such as standard, special or promotional. |
| zip | Observed pricing ZIP as text; blank means not recorded. |
| verified_at | Source verification time in ISO 8601 UTC. |
| source_snapshot | Link to supporting source evidence. |

## Questions

1. Restrict to `term_days == 365`. Show a histogram or empirical cumulative
   distribution for each institution type. Compare medians and sample sizes.
   Why might quoting only the maximum APY be misleading?
2. Compare one-year and five-year medians using every available row at each
   term. Then join those terms on `regulator_id` and plot the within-institution
   difference in APY. Do the two analyses answer the same question?
3. Count how many of the nine terms each regulator contributes. What would go
   wrong if an analysis treated all 3,013 rows as independent institutions?
4. A difference between the two group medians is in percentage points, not
   percent. Express the one-year median difference in both percentage points
   and basis points. Does this observational comparison establish why the
   groups differ, or which offers an individual can open?
